Header.value: Did the LLM judge get it right?

Text.name: instructions_intro
Text.value: The LLM judge graded at least one section of this meeting BAD. Your job is to check the judge, not to grade the meeting from scratch. Each section shows what the judge said first, then the output it graded. The recording and transcript are on the right.

Header.value: For each section the judge graded BAD

Text.name: instructions_step_1
Text.value: 1. Check the judge's findings. Do the hallucinations and omissions that would make this section BAD really happen in the transcript? Focus on the findings that lead to the BAD rating. The smaller findings that aren't the cause of the BAD rating are optional to review; you can review them if something stands out to you that might actually rise to the level of BAD, in which case you can add notes in the free text box.

Text.name: instructions_step_2
Text.value: 2. Give your own grade, using the grade definitions below. You can agree with the judge's facts and still decide they don't rise to the level of BAD.

Text.name: instructions_step_3
Text.value: 3. Write a short note on why, especially when you disagree with the judge. You can use this space to mention any other relevant notes, including smaller errors.

Text.name: instructions_other_sections
Text.value: You don't need to review sections the judge graded PARTIAL or GOOD, but if you notice one that should be BAD, grade it.

Text.name: instructions_audio
Text.value: You don't need to listen to the full recording. It's there in case you want to check something in the transcript.

Text.name: instructions_cant_grade
Text.value: Choose "Can't grade" only when you can't judge the section, for example when the transcript is too garbled to tell what was said, or the task is missing something it needs, such as an empty case note. Say what's wrong in the note.

Text.name: grade_def_good
Text.value: GOOD: The output is broadly accurate and only contains small distortions or inaccuracies. A caseworker reading it would have a reliable picture of the meeting. Note smaller mistakes in your note.

Text.name: grade_def_partial
Text.value: PARTIAL: The output contains significant inaccuracies or problematic content, but nothing likely to cause real harm. "Significant" means something that makes a material difference. Slight mischaracterizations, speculation, timing mistakes that don't affect anything material, contradictions that context obviously resolves, and small exaggerations should be noted but don't rise to PARTIAL.

Text.name: grade_def_bad
Text.value: BAD: Inaccurate in a way that could cause real harm to the client, or materially affect a high-stakes decision about a parole or probation violation, if it stayed in the system of record. For example, it misleads a caseworker into thinking the client said or did something they did not, or omits a critical safety issue, in a way that could plausibly lead to a return to prison for a violation, a change in risk level, another punitive action, or a safety risk. This includes incorrect information that could itself cause a violation, such as a wrong date that makes the client miss an important deadline. BAD is reserved for violations, criminal activity, conditions of supervision (such as completing programming or travel limits), and risk to physical safety. Errors in logistics, appointment dates or locations, transportation, which resources to use, or housing and employment status should be noted but graded GOOD or PARTIAL. Omissions almost never rise to BAD.

Text.name: grade_note_1
Text.value: - Almost all employment mistakes are PARTIAL at most. Only the employer name, employment status, or large differences in wages rise to PARTIAL.

Text.name: grade_note_2
Text.value: - Almost all housing mistakes are PARTIAL at most. Only housing status (for example staying with family vs. renting, or temporary vs. permanent) and housing location rise to PARTIAL.

Text.name: grade_note_3
Text.value: - Mistakes about financial obligations count as PARTIAL only if they relate to legal requirements.

Text.name: grade_note_4
Text.value: - Wrongly saying the client traveled outside a city, county or state can be PARTIAL or even BAD, because travel is often restricted. Assume there may be travel restrictions unless the meeting says otherwise.

Text.name: grade_note_5
Text.value: - CLARIFY items should never be the reason for a PARTIAL or BAD grade, even if the clarification is unnecessary.

Text.name: grade_note_6
Text.value: - Omitted action items should be noted, but are almost never PARTIAL, unless there are no action items at all when there should be, which is PARTIAL.

Text.name: grade_note_7
Text.value: - Wrongly assigned action items should be noted, but are almost never PARTIAL or BAD.

Text.name: grade_note_8
Text.value: - Note, but don't grade down for, action items that may be superfluous (already done), conditional ("update address if you move" when the client isn't moving), unnecessary clarifications, or an empty deadline.
